Dingbat Circled Sans-serif Digit One Symbol

There is no legacy Windows Alt code for Dingbat Circled Sans-serif Digit One because it is not in either the OEM code page 437 or Windows-1252 tables. The Unicode codepoint is U+2780, which you can use as ➀ in HTML, \2780 in CSS, or type with Alt+10112 on Windows (BMP only). If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly. Dingbat Circled Sans-serif Digit One is outside both legacy code pages, which is why U+2780 is the identifier that works across Word, HTML, CSS, Python and JavaScript. Dingbat Circled Sans-serif Digit One has no named HTML entity, so use the numeric escape ➀ or the hex escape ➀.

How to type dingbat circled sans-serif digit one on Windows

  1. Turn Num Lock on so the numeric keypad is active.
  2. Hold the left Alt key.
  3. Type 1 0 1 1 2 on the numeric keypad for the decimal codepoint 10112.
  4. Release Alt. The Dingbat Circled Sans-serif Digit One character (➀) appears.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type dingbat circled sans-serif digit one on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Dingbat Circled Sans-serif Digit One. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Dingbat Circled Sans-Serif Digit One" and click the character to insert it.

How to use dingbat circled sans-serif digit one in code

  • HTML: or
  • CSS: content:"\2780"; ()
  • Python: \u2780 or chr(0x2780)
  • JavaScript: \u2780 or String.fromCodePoint(0x2780)
  • JSON: "\u2780"

Frequently asked questions

Is there an Alt code for ➀?

No legacy Alt code exists for Dingbat Circled Sans-serif Digit One because it is not in code page 437 or Windows-1252. Use the Unicode codepoint U+2780 in HTML, CSS or the Character Viewer instead.

How do I type ➀ without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as ➀, or copy the character directly from this page.

Why does Alt+10112 not work?

Alt+10112 only works on a keyboard with a physical numeric keypad. It also requires the application to accept the numeric-keypad input path. Laptops without a numpad need an alternative method.

What is the Unicode for Dingbat Circled Sans-serif Digit One?

The Unicode codepoint for Dingbat Circled Sans-serif Digit One is U+2780. You can use this value in HTML as ➀, in CSS as \2780, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type ➀ on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+2780, then click it.
